title: Many-sorted functions: terms, substitution, and translation

based_on.title: Many-Sorted First-Order Logic
based_on.venue: CS-E3220: SMT — Satisfiability Modulo Theories, 2020 URL version
based_on.pages: Syntax: Signatures, Variables, Terms, and Atoms, Formulas; Semantics: Structures and Interpretations

summary: Add typed operations and capture-avoiding substitution to many-sorted logic, then retain those operations in a guarded ordinary first-order translation.
abstract: Taking the first element of a list produces an element, while adding an element to a list produces a list. Many-sorted functions record these input and output requirements in the language itself. We build terms with the required sorts and prove that replacing variables by terms of the same sort agrees with evaluating at the corresponding values, even under quantifiers. To translate the resulting logic into ordinary first-order logic, we retain the functions and mark each sort by a predicate. Requiring these predicates to be nonempty and closed under the declared operations lets ordinary models recover genuine sorted models. Both directions preserve satisfaction, so a theory with sorted functions has a model whenever every finite part has one.
